title: Turn on merge_via_rest and fix the test that pinned it off
summary: Add a [landing] table with merge_via_rest = true and a reason comment to athena.toml. Rewrite rest_merge_is_off_unless_the_config_turns_it_on to check the default on a config with the [landing] table removed, and to assert this repository's config turns the merge on.

defaults_applied.how: The test is changed to pin the default, not the live setting.
cargo test and clippy must pass.
Only athena.toml and the one test change.
The comment states the reason for an outside reader.

assumptions: Other tests that append to REPO_CONFIG do not add a [landing] table (the grep shows only the one test does), so they are unaffected.

The [landing] table can be placed anywhere valid in athena.toml, and removing it for the test can be done by text manipulation of the table (a helper that drops the [landing] header and its key lines).

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml contains a [landing] table with merge_via_rest = true, preceded by a comment giving the reason (owner set the repo squash-only with a ruleset on main and approved merging verified work once required checks pass). No other setting changes.

The test no longer asserts REPO_CONFIG lacks [landing]; it builds a config with the [landing] table removed (not by appending a second table, which would be a duplicate) and asserts the default is off.
The test asserts Config::parse(REPO_CONFIG) has landing.merge_via_rest true, and still checks that an explicit true and an empty [landing] table behave as before, using a stripped base.
Run `cargo test --locked`; all tests pass, including config::tests::rest_merge_is_off_unless_the_config_turns_it_on.
Run `cargo clippy --locked` and `cargo fmt --check`; both are clean.

out_of_scope: Other tests or code in config.rs
Repository settings, rulesets, or CI workflows
departures: Slightly cheaper and likelier to pass than the reference: a two-file change with a failing test already diagnosed. The risk is a duplicate [landing] table in other tests or a strip helper that breaks parsing.
